marks.gloss_en: the mishna: a sciatic nerve cooked with the sinews, if not recognised -- all of them are forbidden
the mishna: likewise a piece of a carcass [or of non-kosher fish] cooked with the pieces, if not recognised -- all of them are forbidden
והאי כף מיבעי ליה למעוטי עוף דלית ליה כף -- 'kaf' is already spent on excluding a bird, so how can it also yield Shmuel's dictum?
תרי כף כתיבי -- 'kaf' is written twice [in the verse], one for each
this 'kaf' is needed to exclude a bird, which has no kaf
and R' Yehuda: 'eating' is written of it
and R' Yehuda derives that from 'that is on the kaf of the thigh'
and the Rabbis: that [phrase] is needed for Shmuel's [dictum] -- the Torah forbade only what is on the kaf of the thigh
and the Rabbis: that ['the thigh'] is [the nerve] whose prohibition spreads through the whole thigh
איני? והאמר רב הונא: גדי שצלאו בחלבו אסור לאכול אפילו מראש אזנו -- roasting forbids [the whole]; kind svara under protest: no objection kind for an amoraic-memra contradiction
Rav Huna: a kid roasted with its fat -- it is forbidden to eat even from the tip of its ear
Shmuel: they taught [that the thigh is forbidden] only where [the nerve] was cooked in it
a thigh in which the sciatic nerve was cooked: if there is [enough of it] to impart flavor, it is forbidden
